svg.text: When it breaks — five failures, and what each one actually cost
A job is a chain of checkpointed stages running inside one push request. Every mode below was executed against real infrastructure and written down — none of it is a design claim.
THE DELIVERY CONTRACT — ACKNOWLEDGE ON SUCCESS, NOT ON RECEIPT
Pub/Sub
push subscription, OIDC
ack deadline 600 s
redelivers what is not acked
push
The pipeline runs inside the push request
no background task, no fire-and-forget: the HTTP response is the receipt
for the work, not for the message
request timeout 900 s — the 43.9 s reference batch fits with room to spare
a stage that raises returns 5xx and leaves the delivery unacknowledged
200 — acknowledged
the message is done, the job is completed
5xx, or no reply at all
never acknowledged — Pub/Sub redelivers,
and the job resumes from its checkpoint
redelivered — the only retry the system needs
Why the shape is this way
The first deployment acknowledged at once
and ran the pipeline in a background task.
Cloud Run throttles CPU after the response,
so the engine acked work it could not then
perform — and because it had acked, Pub/Sub
never retried. A live job stalled at
“fetched” and stayed there.
Moving the pipeline inside the request
restored retry semantics for free.
THE JOB AS A STATE MACHINE — EVERY TRANSITION IS A FIRESTORE CHECKPOINT
received
fetched
graded
audited
risk_assessed
synced
verified
optimized
completed
Firestore records the stage and its per-stage status at every transition, so a redelivery skips everything already marked succeeded and re-pays for none of it.
failed — and how a job gets out of it
Any stage that raises marks the job failed and answers 5xx. Only a completed checkpoint is
answered “duplicate”; a checkpoint a dead instance left in any other stage is accepted for
redelivery once it has been idle for 600 s — the gate that used to strand crashed jobs.
Resume, measured on one job delivered three times
41.0 s for the fresh run, then 2.3 s, then 8.0 s. The third delivery’s audit event holds only
Stage_sync, Stage_verify and Stage_optimize — nothing before them was computed twice.
Grading is the expensive stage; a resumed delivery never pays for it a second time.
FIVE WAYS IT BREAKS — EACH ONE RUN, NOT ARGUED
Duplicate delivery
WHAT BREAKS
Pub/Sub is at-least-once: the same message
arrives twice — and eight upload events for
one batch arrive at the same moment.
WHAT HOLDS
The webhook claims the job id in memory
before anything else, so simultaneous
deliveries collapse into one. It then reads
the checkpoint: a completed job is answered
“duplicate” before a task is ever created,
and the runner keeps a second guard of its
own inside the pipeline.
MEASURED
Deployed service, same body POSTed twice:
200 “duplicate” in 0.363 s and 0.274 s.
Checkpoint updated_at unchanged.
1 SIS record and 1 audit event — the same
ones that were already there.
Zero new writes. Zero recompute.
Fan-in on the deployed run: 8 upload
notifications produced exactly 1 job.
The instance dies mid-job
WHAT BREAKS
SIGKILL to the process 26 s into a batch,
with grading finished and the audit stage
just starting. Cloud Run may do this.
WHAT HOLDS
Completed stages are already in Firestore
and the session document holds every
grading result. The delivery was never
acknowledged, so Pub/Sub redelivers; the
run re-enters at the pending stage and
pays nothing for the work it has already
paid for.
MEASURED
Checkpoint survived at stage “graded”, all 3
grading results kept, 0 SIS writes, and curl
reported an empty reply — no ack.
Running the scenario found a real bug: the
gate answered the redelivery “duplicate”
and stranded the job. Fixed — only
“completed” dedupes, idle > 600 s resumes.
A job stuck for a day then finished in 1.7 s.
The SIS is unreachable
WHAT BREAKS
The school system refuses the connection —
or answers, and rejects some records while
accepting others.
WHAT HOLDS
Every record the write was carrying is
parked in the dead-letter queue and the
stage fails with 5xx. On redelivery only the
orphans are re-sent; records the SIS already
accepted are resolved, never posted twice.
An outage does not spend the 3-attempt
budget — only a record-level refusal does.
MEASURED
One job, three deliveries of one event:
1 · dead port → 500, failed at sync, 41.0 s,
zero writes, all 6 records parked.
2 · stub rejects 2 of 6 → 500, 2 dead-letter
entries, 2.3 s — nothing recomputed.
3 · restored → 200, exactly the 2 orphan
documents written, both entries
resolved, 8.0 s.
One exam, not the batch
WHAT BREAKS
A page crashes the grader — a structure the
repair budget cannot fix, or a model error
on that one call.
WHAT HOLDS
The failure is scoped to the exam. The batch
carries on, and the crashed student still
gets a card: “this exam could not be graded
— it needs marking by hand”. The breaker
then measures two ratios against the
manifest roster — quarantined and failed —
and either over 15 % suspends auto-sync.
MEASURED
15 crashes + 1 clean → breaker trips, 15
failure cards, goal not met (pinned test).
16 of 16 crashing → 16 cards, empty ledger,
and the job ends FAILED on purpose: zero
successes is a systemic signal, not a
per-exam one, so it is never acknowledged.
In production 2 of 8 quarantined = 25 %,
over 15 %: the whole batch went to review.
The batch is truncated
WHAT BREAKS
A scan uploads after grading started, or an
object never arrives — and the job would
report success over a short roster.
WHAT HOLDS
The verify stage re-lists the bucket prefix
once and diffs the gradable objects against
the manifest. Missing files become a block
on the verification report, one review card
each (“this scan arrived after grading
started”) and goal_met = false. A listing that
fails degrades to checked:false, never fatal.
MEASURED
Live GCP-mode run: 16 of 16 objects matched
against real Cloud Storage.
Upstream of it the settler waits for uploads
to stop arriving — 5 s rounds, up to 6 —
before the manifest is fixed, so the ordinary
late scan never becomes a truncation at all.
Pinned by scenario test: a file missing from the
batch yields one card and goal_met = false.
Every scenario above was executed, not designed.

Sources: resilience-2026-08-20 (six scenarios, deployed service and local GCP mode) · sync-failure-modes (outage parity, the zero-grade batch) · implementation 012 · offline suite 653 passed / 10 skipped.
